# Second Implementation Delta — Structural Reconciliation

The Awtsmoos renews the second pass before tests can call the structure complete;
Awtsmoos.com therefore measures each vessel, reads each rewritten file, and closes cache/version ambiguity before execution takes its seat.

## Second-Pass Work Completed

- Split Portal interaction binding into `PortalInteractionController.js` with removable listener cleanup.
- Split Portal state-to-DOM manifestation into `PortalStateRenderer.js`.
- Completely rewrote `PortalApp.js` as lifecycle/navigation/loading coordinator with `stop()` cleanup.
- Added compact `PortalTypeRenderer.js`.
- Completely rewrote `PortalUnknownRenderer.js` so collection cards remain compact while detail remains fully generic/inspectable.
- Completely rewrote `PortalBuiltInRenderers.js` to register API-family, Portal-type, collection, inspector, root, and unknown fallbacks deterministically.
- Completely rewrote `PortalBuiltinTypes.js` so the API-family schema follows the real legacy catalog shape `{id, path, description}`.
- Split Portal component styling into `resource.css`, `cards.css`, and `values.css`.
- Completely rewrote `components.css` as a small import composition vessel.
- Added explicit styling for classed `.portal-facts`, preventing specialist Portal markup from bypassing raw semantic fallbacks into browser-default layout.

## Mechanical Line-Count Evidence

- `PortalInteractionController.js`: 53 lines.
- `PortalStateRenderer.js`: 64 lines.
- `PortalApp.js`: 115 lines.
- `PortalBuiltinTypes.js`: 84 lines.
- `PortalTypeRenderer.js`: 61 lines.

Every second-pass source remains below the 120-line ceiling without compressing documentation or implementation.

## Full Second Readback

Every second-pass file above was reread completely after writing. The complete Portal CSS import chain was also reread and every expected imported file exists.

## Closed First-Pass Deltas

- Controller responsibility/size: closed.
- Component CSS responsibility/size: closed.
- API-family `key` versus `id` schema mismatch: closed.
- Heavy Portal-type collection cards: closed.
- Heavy unknown collection cards: closed.
- Unremovable document interaction listener: closed.

## Remaining Architectural Extension Point

`PortalFieldRegistry.js` remains intentionally present but not yet used to transform arbitrary values based on type semantic metadata. This is not hidden runtime behavior: the proof surface uses safe bounded generic rendering plus exact API-family/type renderers. Semantic-role integration belongs after the current type-definition/read path is runtime-proven, so a field-role system is not guessed against unverified schemas.

## Newly Discovered Delta — Cache Version Coherence

The second-pass component graph uses `portal-ui-002`, but:

- `geelooy/portal/portal.css` still imports its first-level styles with `portal-ui-001`.
- `geelooy/portal/index.html` still links `portal.css` and `portal.js` with `portal-ui-001`.

A fresh browser would still obtain the current new untracked files, but leaving two cache epochs in one release weakens deployment diagnosis and can preserve stale first-pass resources in an already-open browser.

### Required third write pass

Completely rewrite:

- `geelooy/portal/portal.css` to use `portal-ui-002` for all first-level imports.
- `geelooy/portal/index.html` to request `portal.css?v=portal-ui-002` and `portal.js?v=portal-ui-002`.

Then reread those two files and verify the complete Portal dependency graph has one cache epoch.

## Verification Gate After Third Pass

Only after that small coherence pass may testing begin:

1. create focused Portal contract/adapter/service tests,
2. run syntax checks,
3. run Node tests,
4. probe real local HTTP API routes,
5. probe CompactJS and the previously missing UI modules,
6. run Chrome runtime/UI audits on `/apps/` and `/portal/` at desktop and mobile sizes.

## NEXT_ACTION

Rewrite `portal.css` and `index.html` completely with cache epoch `portal-ui-002`, reread them, then create the Portal test universe before executing any tests.
